_comment: Declared attributes no platform converter reads. Hand-maintained: close a gap by implementing it (then delete the entry) or by narrowing platform/mode in attribute_definitions.json. reason is one of: dynamic-key, legacy, platform-na, runtime-only, unimplemented.

entries.note: ios dynamic implements it (SwiftJsonUI CollectionConverter.swift:662 / TableConverter.swift:46,49); no codegen face reads it. Not "unimplemented" — this scan only walks the Ruby codegen. attribute_semantics.json -> collectionSeparators (plan 51-E).

Was runtime-only while no codegen face read it; B implemented the ios codegen face against the enum (collection_converter.rb LIST_STYLES), so android and web are now a genuine implementation gap. attribute_semantics.json -> collectionSeparators (plan 51-E).
codegen 未対応。ランタイム側に実装あり (ios: UIKit) — この検査は Ruby codegen しか走査しないので、実装の有無ではなく codegen 対応の有無を表す

UIKit-only KVC binding (SJUIViewCreator sets view.binding / bindingSet). The last Ruby reader was sjui's table_converter.rb, folded into the Collection route when 49-E ruled Table is a Collection — so this became unread by that ruling, not by anything failing. The declaration says it is superseded by `@{...}` in the attribute value itself; the UIKit runtime still honours it for layouts that predate that, which is why it is not deleted. Reason `legacy` rather than `unimplemented`: nothing is missing.
